mbm-2601.clue: I was the coat check until the band played that one.
mbm-2601.quote: At my first ballroom social I was happy watching the coats. The drummer came off for a break and taught me a box step between the racks. Now I take the first shift so I can dance the rest.

mbm-2602.clue: I counted five yellow circles on the way down.
mbm-2602.quote: Under my open parachute the hay bales looked like coins on green felt. From the ground I walked back to look. One was an empty paddling pool. The sky still owes me change.

mbm-2603.clue: The kettle is seventy years older than the tent.
mbm-2603.quote: I inherited a soot-black camp kettle that sings through a dent. At night I set it outside our new tent. You could mistake the kettle and the stars for the whole camp my grandad slept in.

mbm-2604.clue: We beat the game by trading thumbs.
mbm-2604.quote: I could steer the little spaceship but couldn't fire quickly. My cousin held the controller from the other side. When the last pixel winked out neither of us knew whose high score to sign.

mbm-2605.clue: I found gravity in the bread bin.
mbm-2605.quote: I practiced juggling with rolls from the bread bin while my little brother counted catches. At thirty I dropped one straight into his bowl of soup. He started cheering for shorter runs.

mbm-2606.quote: I polished two wooden juggling balls but left the first one rough. When the lights are low I can feel which throw started the pattern. That's when I let myself look at the people smiling.

mbm-2607.clue: The black square is on the wrong side of the river.
mbm-2607.quote: I turned one patch upside down. My grandfather looked at the quilt and said our old ferry always drifted that way. I put a red stitch where he remembered the dock.

mbm-2608.clue: I can count the visitors after breakfast.
mbm-2608.quote: I leave a patch of smooth dirt beside the tent flap. In the morning we read the tracks. One night a mouse walked right through a rabbit print like a little guest arriving late.

mbm-2609.clue: I once played a squeaky gate from behind a curtain.
mbm-2609.quote: The gate prop broke before curtain up. I made the noise myself, and the lead actor stopped to oil an invisible hinge. The audience clapped for a gate that wasn't there.

mbm-2610.clue: I have a list of things that weren't hawks.
mbm-2610.quote: A brown grocery bag, three kites and a runaway hat all fooled me this year. I drew each underneath the hawks in my field journal. The hat is catching a splendid thermal.

mbm-2611.clue: Our slow waltz starts at the dish rack.
mbm-2611.quote: My partner dries the last plate, takes my hand and turns between the sink and table. When our song ends everything is clean except two circles of flour beneath our shoes.

mbm-2612.clue: I used the label as the center square.
mbm-2612.quote: Everyone gave me scraps for the quilt but my dad had already mended his only spare shirt. He cut off the small maker's label. It sits dead center like the signature on a painting.

mbm-2613.clue: I remember the round by its smells.
mbm-2613.quote: Pine sap at the first tee, frying onions by the sixth, cut grass all the way home. I drew a little frying pan instead of writing my score on six. We stopped there afterward for onions.

mbm-2614.clue: The commercial break can last all winter.
mbm-2614.quote: We taped a TV special one snow day. You can hear Mum's boots in the room whenever we play it back. We always sit through the old ads, waiting for the sound of the snow coming in.

mbm-2615.clue: We play round the washing line.
mbm-2615.quote: The rule is you must throw the disc under one wet sheet and over the next. My sister keeps adding laundry. By Sunday we've invented a tournament and dried all the towels.

mbm-2616.clue: The wall label I remember was handwritten.
mbm-2616.quote: A museum drawer held the pencil its owner used to label a shell collection. The pencil was sharpened down to a stub. I spent more time looking at that stub than at all the lovely shells.

mbm-2617.clue: I give the river back its pebble.
mbm-2617.quote: My cousin packed a smooth stone from our first rafting trip. She forgot her life jacket pocket had a hole. At the takeout she grinned and said the river must have recognized it.

mbm-2618.quote: I made a jar whose lid only settles when the blue glaze spots line up. My flatmates named the right spot Tuesday. Whenever somebody wants sugar they ask if it's Tuesday yet.

mbm-2619.clue: My rival's trophy is upside down.
mbm-2619.quote: My friend drew a tiny trophy on a paper high-score flag and taped it to my TV upside down. I beat the score that night. I turned the flag round anyway. It looks better that way.

mbm-2620.clue: I learned to steer by watching a leaf.
mbm-2620.quote: My daughter set a maple leaf on the water beside our canoe and asked me to go its speed. For ten minutes I had to stop muscling the paddle. That leaf taught me a better stroke.

mbm-2621.clue: The best photo was in the corner.
mbm-2621.quote: I photographed a huge bridge. In the bottom corner my dad was tying my niece's shoelace. I printed just that corner for her bedroom. The bridge gets a narrow strip of blue paint.

mbm-2622.clue: I always buy the bent pencil.
mbm-2622.quote: The miniature golf counter has a tin of short pencils. I pick one with bite marks for luck. My friend swears the pencil remembers our last round and won't let me make the same mistake twice.

mbm-2623.clue: My first jump souvenir was a sock.
mbm-2623.quote: My sister knitted red socks for my skydive so she'd spot my feet when I landed. All she noticed from the fence was the huge blue canopy. I showed her the socks from much closer.

mbm-2624.clue: I copied the curve from a spoon.
mbm-2624.quote: The ski trail beside our lodge bends in one long silver S. Back at breakfast I pulled a spoon through yogurt to show the turn. My niece ate the entire black diamond with peaches.

mbm-2625.clue: I collect the view from the wrong exit.
mbm-2625.quote: I took the service stairs by mistake and found a little balcony over a square full of oranges. I ask for the plain staircase first now. The grand entrance is always easy to find afterward.
